Probability theory (Bayes' theorem) formalizes Bayesian inference (Wikipedia Bayesian inference: "computes the posterior probability according to Bayes' theorem"; SEP Bayes' Theorem: "relates the 'direct' probability of a hypothesis conditional on a given body of data ... to the 'inverse' probability of the data conditional on the hypothesis"). Probability theory (stochastic processes) formalizes the asset-pricing / decision-under-uncertainty core of financial economics (Wikipedia Mathematical finance: derivatives pricing uses "risk-neutral probability ... continuous-time martingales ... Itō calculus, PDEs"; Wikipedia Financial economics: "centers on decision making under uncertainty in the context of the financial markets"). Probability theory is the formal substrate of information theory — entropy is a functional of a probability distribution (Wikipedia Information theory: "Information theory is based on probability theory and statistics"; nLab entropy: "We can give a precise mathematical definition of the entropy in probability theory. Fix a probability space (X,μ)"). `formalizes` not `part_of`: information theory is a distinct field built on probability, not a subdomain of it.

Probability theory formalizes the probability-distribution concept as a probability measure under Kolmogorov axioms (EoM: "Any such measure ... is called a probability distribution ... basic in the axiomatics introduced by A.N. Kolmogorov in 1933"; Wikipedia: "a probability measure on (X,A)"). The concept is partly internal to probability theory — a tight, near-definitional formalization (low information content, recorded).

Probability theory (measure-theoretic, Kolmogorov 1933) gives the random-variable concept its formal definition as a measurable function on a probability space (EoM: "a random variable is nothing but a measurable function on a probability space"; nLab: "The formalization of this idea in modern probability theory (Kolmogorov 33) is to take a random variable to be a measurable function").

Probability theory is the formal substrate of the statistical-mechanics ensemble formalism (Wikipedia Statistical mechanics: macroscopic properties explained via microscopic parameters "characterized by probability distributions"; "The statistical ensemble is a probability distribution over all possible states"; nLab statistical mechanics: "an ensemble may be a probability distribution of similar physical systems"). Gibbs/Boltzmann.

Probability theory provides the formal/mathematical foundation for (mathematical) statistics — estimation and hypothesis testing rest on it (Wikipedia: "Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory ... to statistics"; EoM Mathematical statistics: methods of estimation/testing are "based on probability theory"). Distinct from the prerequisite_for edge (a learning order); descriptive statistics is less probability-dependent (scope caveat).
